summary: Today’s pulse tracks Trump touts primary success after Republicans win elections in South Carolina and Oklahoma – live, Women using HRT at lower risk of dementia, study suggests, and Duke and Duchess of Sussex have arrived back in UK, say reports. Across Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are people, dementia, and nicola. In the background, Channel 5 drama to examine how Nicola Sturgeon’s ex-husband stole SNP funds and Burnham announces plan for 10,000 work experience placements for young people – UK politics live keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Trump touts primary success after Republicans win elections in South Carolina and Oklahoma – live
headlines.description: Sister of late Lindsey Graham, who has been backed by Trump, overcomes concern about lack of experience to win place on November ballot Darline Graham wins Republican primary for US Senate US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) said in a post on X that the strike targeted a vessel “operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Caribbean.”

headlines.title: Women using HRT at lower risk of dementia, study suggests
headlines.description: Scientists found those who had used hormone replacement therapy were 10% less likely to be diagnosed with dementia Hormone replacement therapy may reduce the risk of dementia, a study has found. Scientists tracked more than 180,000 postmenopausal women in the UK in the largest study of its kind. They found that those who had used HRT were 10% less likely to develop any type of dementia and 16% less likely to be diagnosed with Alzheimer’s, the most common form, compared with those who had never used it.

headlines.title: Duke and Duchess of Sussex have arrived back in UK, say reports
headlines.description: Harry, Meghan and family expected to enjoy ‘extended stay’ with children Archie and Lilibet already enrolled at school The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have arrived back in the UK, landing at Birmingham airport, according to reports. Prince Harry, Meghan, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, are expected to enjoy an “extended stay” in Britain, with the children already enrolled at school in the UK and due to start next week.

headlines.title: Channel 5 drama to examine how Nicola Sturgeon’s ex-husband stole SNP funds
headlines.description: To Nicola, Love Peter will focus on couple’s relationship during 12-year period of embezzlement and fallout of case Channel 5 is reuniting with the producers of Power: the Downfall of Huw Edwards for a drama about how Nicola Sturgeon’s estranged husband embezzled £400,000 from the Scottish National party and the impact it had on her reputation. To Nicola, Love Peter will examine the couple’s relationship over the 12-year period that Peter Murrell diverted funds from the SNP while he was the chief executive to spend on items including a £124,550 motorhome and more than £2,600 on a pair of luxury salt and pepper grinders.

headlines.title: Burnham announces plan for 10,000 work experience placements for young people – UK politics live
headlines.description: Prime minister spoke to press while on visit to a Sainsbury’s supermarket in London this morning Over 40,000 more people died on the hottest days in England between 1988 and 2025 than would be expected, according to data published by the Office for National Statistics on Wednesday. The figures do not include this summer, when England has sweltered under a succession of heatwaves and is on track to record its highest ever number of heat-related deaths . The UK Health Security Agency announced on 30 July that an estimated 2,877 people had died in the May and June heatwaves alone. The total is almost double the figure for the whole summer in 2025.

headlines.title: ‘Major casualties’ feared after flash floods along Nepal-Tibet border
headlines.description: Hundreds missing and at least 22 people dead after floods sweep away houses, roads, bridges and power projects Hundreds are missing and at least 22 people have died after torrential floods ⁠hit the Himalayan border areas of ⁠Nepal and in ​Tibet in China. Houses, roads, bridges and power projects were swept away ⁠in Nepal while officials in Tibet said they feared “major casualties” with some missing in the county of Gyirong after a mudslide hit a land crossing between the neighbours.

headlinePool.title: First Thing: Pause on US immigrant visa leaves thousands of applicants in limbo
headlinePool.description: All US immigrant visa applications halted as state department moves to tighten restrictions and limit access. Plus tributes pour in for Dolly Parton, who has died aged 80 Good morning. All US immigrant visa applications have been paused by the Trump administration as the state department moves to tighten restrictions and limit access to applicants whom they deem could need US assistance. The agency launched the initiative at all embassies and consulates in early August. Applicants with scheduled interviews were sent emails that their appointments had been canceled. Agency officials claim this will ensure visa applicants will not end up relying on US public benefits. This week the Trump administration also announced plans to revoke visas from asylum seekers who had initially entered the US for tourism or business. Up to 200,000 people seeking asylum could be affected. Is the move lawful? “The court made clear that immigration laws cannot be used to justify discrimination,” Joanna Cuevas Ingram, a senior staff attorney at the National Immigration Law Center, said. In February, a federal judge overturned the president’s attempt to suspend the US refugee system entirely. Why are the states suing Meta? The lawsuit centers on the allegations that Meta deliberately designed addictive products that hooked young people, leading to mental health issues, including anxiety, depression and suicide. Meta has denied all allegations, saying the states are chasing an “outlandish payout”.

headlinePool.description: A hospital official told the BBC that the door to the ward was not locked, but manned with security guards, to protect the babies.

headlinePool.title: China advises its citizens to leave Taiwan ally Eswatini over 'security risks'
headlinePool.description: Eswatini is one of 12 countries, and the only one in Africa, that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan.

headlinePool.title: Murder investigation launched after two die in Middlesbrough house fire
headlinePool.description: Cleveland police not ruling out links to organised crime, as fire comes amid force’s investigation into fatal A66 crash A murder investigation has been launched after a house fire in Middlesbrough killed two people, with police not ruling out links to organised crime. The blaze in the early hours of Wednesday came as police continued to investigate the wider circumstances around a collision on Saturday on the A66 that killed seven people, including two police officers.

headlinePool.title: Hope and concern swirls for Ohioans around ‘world’s largest datacenter’
headlinePool.description: Piketon datacenter promises to generate thousands of jobs, but environmental groups voice concern over project On a winding road tucked away behind forests in the Appalachian foothills of southern Ohio is where OpenAI, Nvidia and Japanese investors are set to spend $500bn on one of the largest artificial intelligence datacenters on the planet. Last March, the energy secretary, Chris Wright, the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick and a host of Japanese and other dignitaries briefly descended on Piketon to enthusiastically break ground on a project to build 8GW worth of AI computing power.
